question: What is 'lectio divina' and what are its four traditional steps?

choices.A: Sacred reading of Scripture in four steps: lectio (read), meditatio (meditate), oratio (pray), contemplatio (contemplate)
choices.B: A Latin Mass practice involving four Scripture readings at each liturgy
choices.C: A novena prayer practice: nine days of reading, nine days of fasting, nine days of Communion, nine days of adoration
choices.D: A Benedictine practice of reciting all 150 Psalms divided into four weekly cycles

teaching.title: Lectio Divina
teaching.body: Lectio divina ('sacred reading') is an ancient monastic practice of prayerful Scripture reading. Guigo II, a 12th-century Carthusian, systematized four rungs of a 'ladder': (1) Lectio — reading the text slowly and attentively; (2) Meditatio — ruminating on the text, listening for what God is saying; (3) Oratio — responding to God in personal prayer arising from the text; (4) Contemplatio — resting silently in God's presence, beyond words. Some add a fifth step: Actio (action) — living out what was received. Vatican II's Dei Verbum 25 encouraged clergy and laity to practice lectio divina regularly.
